scope: Proposition 4.4 (Good-prime norms and rectangular filling) of the manuscript “The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one” (preprints/The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 002 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 734e4050dc8416c0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 28. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For either order pattern, adjoining a fresh prime ℓ ∤ cdn2L to both orders and to M gives, after the elliptic projection, the rational norm multiplier 1 − aℓ(f)[ℓ] ℓ + [ℓ]2 ℓ . The trace defining this norm is integral. At complete splitting in a lower abelian field the scalar is det(1 − ρT (Frℓ))/ℓ. In rectangular order, let qa 0 ∥ b, q0 ∤ b1. At a finite even field character ν of conductor dividing M, filling qa 0 into the first row gives the rational identity zfilled = 1 − aq0 (f)ν(q0)/q0  zbefore.
